A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MergeMix work. The text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification and MLLM experiments, including calibration, occlusion robustness, ablations and token-reduction evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds audio classification, CAFormer results, preference-scoring evaluations and inference-efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The token-merging, attention-recovery and image-mixing pipeline is retained. Equation (11) changes the stated preference margin from 1−λ to 1−λ̂, using the re-scaled ratio. However, new Algorithm 2 subtracts λ instead, leaving the implemented margin unclear.

E1.justification: V2 retains the image-classification and visual-language datasets and adds environmental sound classification on ESC-50 and UrbanSound8K with HuBERT-Base (Appendix C.3, Table A8). This extends actual evaluation to a distinct audio modality and task domain.

E2.justification: TdAttenMix is added to the CIFAR100 and Stanford-Cars comparisons in Tables 1–2. New Table A13 adds mDPO, printed as mDOP, Re-Align and vanilla SimPO as ranking-loss comparators. The original comparator rows remain.

E3.justification: V2 introduces HuBERT audio fine-tuning for 100 epochs, CAFormer-S12 evaluation, MLLM/human reward scoring across mixing ratios, and A100 profiling of latency and component overhead across merge ratios. These expand the evaluation design; the original benchmark settings are retained. The judging protocol lacks sample counts and prompts.

E4.justification: V2 adds tests of the mixing-ratio/preference relationship (Figure A2), a ranking-loss ablation (Table A13), efficiency sensitivity analyses (Tables A14–A15), and Grad-CAM and additional case-study evidence. Original calibration, occlusion and token-ratio analyses remain; Figure A3 redisplays existing token-ratio results.

E5.justification: Table A8 introduces ± quantities for audio results, such as 76.51±0.95 on ESC-50, whereas v1's result tables report point estimates. V2 does not define these uncertainty quantities or provide run counts, seeds or significance tests.

E6.justification: Retained numerical table entries are unchanged, but v2 adds baseline, audio, backbone, preference and efficiency results. Examples include audio means of 76.51 and 85.69 and CAFormer accuracy of 84.30 versus CutMix's 84.69. Table A13 also introduces an inconsistent MergeMix aggregate: its four scores average 60.42, not the reported 61.29.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 adds explicit Gaussian parameter definitions, mean=K/L and std=p/∑M, where v1 supplied verbal ratio descriptions. Together with the revised preference-margin expression, this changes the mathematical specification locally. No theorem, proof or new complexity argument is added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a unified token-merging augmentation for classification and preference-based MLLM alignment, with accuracy, efficiency and generalization benefits. V2 foregrounds label re-scaling and adaptive SimPO margins in its abstract and contributions, but these components and claims already appear in v1.

C2.justification: V2 interprets judge-score monotonicity as support for a human-preference proxy, attributes CAFormer's second-place performance to limited attention stages, and discusses inference tradeoffs. Existing image-only augmentation and static-merging limitations remain. Its new interpretation that the mixed loss outperforms vanilla SimPO is undermined by Table A13's arithmetic.

D1.justification: V2 adds pseudocode for both applications, explicit Gaussian parameters, audio implementation settings and profiling hardware information. It removes v1's explicit random 16×16 patch-masking description for the retained occlusion tests. Existing code-access information and principal training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work adds DiffuseMix, GenMix and recent token-compression references, alongside citations supporting the new experiments and comparators. The Naseer et al. occlusion reference is removed. The existing related-work taxonomy and overall research positioning remain.

P1.justification: The abstract and contribution paragraphs are rewritten, selected prose is polished, and appendices are reorganized into details, classification, visual understanding, efficiency and visualization sections. The main narrative and most retained explanations remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds five appendix tables, expands Figure 3 with a case study, and adds preference-score plots, a visualization of retained token-ratio results and Grad-CAM figures. Main Figure 5 changes to a Grad-CAM display while occlusion plots remain in Figure A1. Numerous retained displays are resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful audio/backbone coverage and inference-efficiency evidence. However, its new central loss ablation reports a MergeMix average of 61.29 although the listed scores average 60.42, undermining the claimed advantage over vanilla SimPO. New Algorithm 2 also conflicts with Equation (11)'s margin. These problems affect validation and implementation guidance, so the benefits and harms do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
